_doc: NPC_AI_SPEC §5.1 / §12 — which intrinsic actions an archetype offers and
which need profile (needs.json) drives it.
`intrinsic` is CONTENT, not code: phase 1 stores the list on the agent and
the debug overlay prints it. The UtilityReasoner (phase 5) is what turns
these ids into scored candidates, alongside affordance-derived actions.
Updated 2026-07-28 (phase 5.3, found missing during the phase-5
validation pass): villager gained flee_to_safety/sleep/gather_resource/
haul_to_deposit (5.6/5.7's own action ids, none of which existed here
before — gather_resource and haul_to_deposit only ever apply once a
villager has a job, gated at candidate-assembly time, not by archetype).
guard's 'flee' renamed to 'flee_to_safety' to match §5.6's real id — it
was never consumed by any live code, confirmed via grep, so this is a
content fix, not a behavior change. guard intentionally did NOT gain
'sleep': defenders keep the OPPOSITE hours to working villagers
(isWatchHours, data/villagers.ts) and are driven separately by
Defenders.tsx, not by this reasoner yet — whether/how a guard rests is
an open question for whenever defender AI actually gets built, not
something to silently assume works the same way as a villager's night.
Updated 2026-08-03: villager gained idle_fidget/notice_player (ambient.ts/
notice.ts) — real ambient-category/social-category content, both scored
so low they only ever win during genuine downtime (see those files' own
headers). New 'court' archetype: ONLY those same two actions, nothing
movement/schedule-related — deliberately narrower than villager so a
court NPC (King Leo, Richard, Storm, the starter farmers — anyone
courtAmbientSync.ts spawns an Agent for) can never wander off post or
flee a raid three regions away, while still reading as alive via the
same fidget/notice content a working villager gets.
